answer: Nonce-bound attestation chains. Each new agent identity must embed the hash of a fresh challenge whose preimage includes a dune survey timestamp signed by the requester, so replaying an old reply fails verification. The chain anchor must also commit to a timber batch serial, forcing every registration to consume a unique physical shipment record that costs the attacker a real procurement and audit trail. A juniper oil lot code then seals the chain terminus, and because each code is single-use the attacker pays full material and logging cost per identity, not a reusable token.
